_help: Quiz for Spot the Scam. 5 to 8 questions. answer must match one of the options exactly. explain is shown after the quiz. This folder is never shown to visitors.

questions.question: Someone asks for your seed phrase to "verify" your wallet. What is it?
options: A scam: nobody real ever needs your seed phrase
Fine if they are from support
Fine if they have a blue tick
questions.answer: A scam: nobody real ever needs your seed phrase
questions.explain: Your seed phrase is the key to all your crypto. Real support never asks for it.

questions.question: A message says you won an airdrop, but you must pay a small fee to unlock it. What is that?
options: A tax you have to pay
questions.explain: Real airdrops do not ask you to send money first.

questions.question: A link looks like a famous exchange, but one letter is different. What should you do?
options: Do not click it; type the address yourself or use your bookmark
Click it quickly before the offer ends
questions.answer: Do not click it; type the address yourself or use your bookmark
questions.explain: Look-alike addresses are one of the most common ways to steal logins.

questions.question: "Guaranteed 5% a day, no risk." What does this promise tell you?
options: It is almost certainly a scam
It is a safe savings account
questions.answer: It is almost certainly a scam
questions.explain: No real investment can promise high returns with no risk.

questions.question: A stranger asks you to move the chat to Telegram and open a file for a job. What is the safe move?
options: Do not open the file on a computer that holds your crypto
Open it to see the job
questions.answer: Do not open the file on a computer that holds your crypto
questions.explain: Fake job offers are a common way to plant software that steals wallets.

questions.question: Which one is a red flag in any crypto message?
options: A link to the official website you already know
questions.explain: "Act now" and "last chance" are there to stop you from thinking.
